content.prompt: Find expressions using the laws, then confirm your answer using the parallelogram diagram.

spec.description: Unmarked parallelogram ABCD with horizontal opposite sides; B and C lie above and to the right of A and D respectively.
spec.mathematics: Boundary order A–B–C–D; no diagonals or vector arrows.

answer.worked: $\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}$ by the triangle law: follow A to B to C.
$\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CB}=\overrightarrow{AB}$ by the triangle law: follow A to C to B.
$\overrightarrow{AC}-\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{BC}$. For vectors with common tail A, the difference runs from B to C; in the parallelogram it also equals $\overrightarrow{AD}$.
$\overrightarrow{AD}-\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{BD}$. For vectors with common tail A, the difference runs from the head B of the second vector to the head D of the first.

spec.description: Rotated unmarked parallelogram: P left, Q upper right, S right and R lower left.
spec.mathematics: Boundary order P–Q–S–R. QR and PS are diagonals, not boundary edges. No arrows or diagonals are drawn.

answer.worked: $\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QS}=\overrightarrow{PS}$ by the triangle law: follow P to Q to S.
$\overrightarrow{QR}+\overrightarrow{RS}=\overrightarrow{QS}$ by the triangle law: follow Q to R to S.
$\overrightarrow{PS}-\overrightarrow{PQ}=\overrightarrow{QS}$. For vectors with common tail P, the difference runs from Q to S; it also equals $\overrightarrow{PR}$.
$\overrightarrow{SR}-\overrightarrow{SQ}=\overrightarrow{QR}$. For vectors with common tail S, the difference runs from Q to R.

content.prompt: Prove that:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}+\overrightarrow{CD}\\&=\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CD}\\&=\overrightarrow{AD}\\&=\mathrm{RHS}\end{aligned}$$
Use the negative vector law, then the triangle law twice.

$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\overrightarrow{RT}-\overrightarrow{TR}\\&=\overrightarrow{RT}+\overrightarrow{RT}\\&=2\overrightarrow{RT}\\&=\mathrm{RHS}\end{aligned}$$
Use the parallelogram law of subtraction, then the negative vector law.

$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QR}-\overrightarrow{SR}\\&=\overrightarrow{PR}-\overrightarrow{SR}\\&=\overrightarrow{PR}+\overrightarrow{RS}\\&=\overrightarrow{PS}\\&=\mathrm{RHS}\end{aligned}$$
Use the parallelogram law of subtraction, the triangle law and the negative vector law.

$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\overrightarrow{GH}+\overrightarrow{EF}+\overrightarrow{HE}+\overrightarrow{FG}\\&=\overrightarrow{GH}+\overrightarrow{HE}+\overrightarrow{EF}+\overrightarrow{FG}\\&=\overrightarrow{GE}+\overrightarrow{EG}\\&=\underset{\sim}{0}\\&=\mathrm{RHS}\end{aligned}$$
Use the negative vector law, reorder using the commutative law, then apply the triangle law. Opposite vectors sum to the zero vector.

content.prompt: Given parallelogram $ABCD$, write the vector that is:

spec.description: Parallelogram with A above, B right, C below and D left; both diagonals are drawn and their intersection is unlabelled. Source blue outlines become ordinary black house-style geometry.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a parallelogram. Diagonals AC and DB connect opposite vertices. No lengths or additional marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and vertex labels remain visible in the question edition.

answer.worked: $\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}$ by the triangle law.
$\overrightarrow{AD}+\overrightarrow{DB}=\overrightarrow{AB}$ by the triangle law.
$\overrightarrow{DC}+\overrightarrow{CA}=\overrightarrow{DA}$ by the triangle law.

Opposite sides give $\overrightarrow{CB}=\overrightarrow{DA}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{CD}+\overrightarrow{CB}&=\overrightarrow{CD}+\overrightarrow{DA}\\\overrightarrow{CD}+\overrightarrow{CB}&=\overrightarrow{CA}\end{aligned}$$

Opposite sides give $\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CD}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{DA}-\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{DA}+\overrightarrow{BA}\\\overrightarrow{DA}-\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{CD}+\overrightarrow{DA}\\\overrightarrow{DA}-\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{CA}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}-\overrightarrow{AD}&=\overrightarrow{DA}+\overrightarrow{AB}\\\overrightarrow{AB}-\overrightarrow{AD}&=\overrightarrow{DB}\end{aligned}$$

Opposite sides give $\overrightarrow{DC}=\overrightarrow{AB}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{BC}-\overrightarrow{CD}&=\overrightarrow{BC}+\overrightarrow{DC}\\\overrightarrow{BC}-\overrightarrow{CD}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\\\overrightarrow{BC}-\overrightarrow{CD}&=\overrightarrow{AC}\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt: In the diagram, $\overrightarrow{WX}=\overrightarrow{ZY}$. Explain why $WXYZ$ is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Slanted quadrilateral WXYZ with rightward endpoint arrows from W to X and Z to Y. Connecting sides use thin black strokes instead of source grey.
spec.mathematics: The two supplied directed opposite sides have equal magnitude and direction. Both arrowheads and their endpoints are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: The entire diagram is supplied; no conclusion or solution annotation appears in the question figure.

answer.short: Equal vectors have the same magnitude and direction, so opposite sides $WX$ and $ZY$ are equal and parallel. Therefore $WXYZ$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked: Since $\overrightarrow{WX}=\overrightarrow{ZY}$, sides $WX$ and $ZY$ have the same length and are parallel. A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram. Hence $WXYZ$ is a parallelogram.

What type of special quadrilateral is ABCD? Give reasons for your answer.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral with A upper left, B lower left, C lower right and D upper right; arrows B to A, C to D and A to D. Ordinary source strokes use house black.

answer.short: Rectangle. Opposite sides BA and CD are equal and parallel, and $\angle BAD=90^\circ$.
answer.worked: Since $\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CD}$, opposite sides BA and CD are parallel and equal. Hence ABCD is a parallelogram. Also, $\overrightarrow{BA}\perp\overrightarrow{AD}$ gives $\angle BAD=90^\circ$. A parallelogram with a right angle is a rectangle.

content.prompt: In each part, draw a diagram showing the displacement vector $\overrightarrow{AC}$. Then calculate the magnitude and direction of $\overrightarrow{AC}$. Give magnitude correct to the nearest km where necessary, and direction as a true bearing correct to the nearest degree where necessary.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sarah drives 100 km east from A to B, and then 40 km west from B to C.

answer.worked:
Taking east as positive,
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AC}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\\&=100-40\\&=60\text{ km east}.\end{aligned}$$
The magnitude is $60\text{ km}$ and the true bearing is $090^\circ\text{T}$.

spec.description: Collinear journey with C between A and B; offset arrows distinguish the return leg and displacement.
spec.mathematics: AB is 100 km east, BC is 40 km west, AC is 60 km east.

children.label: b
children.prompt: William walks 6 km south from A to B, and then 4 km east from B to C.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{AC}|&=\sqrt{6^2+4^2}\\&=\sqrt{52}\text{ km}\\&\approx7\text{ km}.\end{aligned}$$
Let $\theta$ be the angle east of south.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{4}{6}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{6}\right).\end{aligned}$$
The true bearing is $180^\circ-\tan^{-1}(4/6)\approx146^\circ\text{T}$.

spec.description: Head-to-tail south and east legs with resultant from A to C, north direction and angle east of south.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,0), B=(0,-6), C=(4,-6); displacement magnitude sqrt(52), bearing 146 degrees rounded.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A boat sails 25 km east from A to B, and then 15 km northeast from B to C.

answer.worked:
Resolve the northeast leg into east and north components.
$$\begin{aligned}E&=25+15\cos45^\circ\\&=25+\frac{15\sqrt2}{2},\\N&=15\sin45^\circ\\&=\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{AC}|&=\sqrt{\left(25+\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2}\\&\approx37\text{ km}.\end{aligned}$$
The true bearing is
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{25+15\sqrt2/2}{15\sqrt2/2}\right)\approx073^\circ\text{T}.$$

spec.description: Unshaded parallelogram with midpoint direction arrows on AB and BC; no diagonals.
spec.mathematics: A bottom left, B top left, C top right, D bottom right; AB labelled a and BC labelled b.

answer.worked:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram have equal lengths. The vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{DC}$ also have the same direction, as do $\overrightarrow{AD}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$, so these two statements are true.

$\overrightarrow{BC}=-\overrightarrow{DA}$, so the second statement is false. Also, $\overrightarrow{AC}=a+b$ whereas $\overrightarrow{DB}=a-b$, so the fourth statement is false.

content.prompt: On the grid of congruent parallelograms, $\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}=\underset{\sim}{b}$.

spec.description: Four columns and two rows of congruent parallelograms, all fifteen labelled intersections and two basis-vector arrows.

children.prompt: Write these vectors in terms of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

answer.worked: $\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$, as given.
$\overrightarrow{OB}=\underset{\sim}{b}$, as given.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OE}&=\overrightarrow{OB}+\overrightarrow{BE}\\&=\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{b}\\&=2\underset{\sim}{b}.\end{aligned}$$
$\overrightarrow{OF}$ consists of three steps in the direction of $\underset{\sim}{a}$, so $\overrightarrow{OF}=3\underset{\sim}{a}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OD}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AD}\\&=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OH}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AH}\\&=\underset{\sim}{a}+2\underset{\sim}{b}.\end{aligned}$$

Follow $H\to M\to J$: two steps in the $\underset{\sim}{a}$ direction and one reversed $\underset{\sim}{b}$ step.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{HJ}&=\overrightarrow{HM}+\overrightarrow{MJ}\\&=2\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}.\end{aligned}$$

Follow $J\to F\to A$: one reversed $\underset{\sim}{b}$ step and two reversed $\underset{\sim}{a}$ steps.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{JA}&=\overrightarrow{JF}+\overrightarrow{FA}\\&=-\underset{\sim}{b}-2\underset{\sim}{a}\\&=-2\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AC}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\quad(\triangle\text{ law})\\\overrightarrow{AC}&=(2\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})+(2\underset{\sim}{a}-3\underset{\sim}{b})\\\overrightarrow{AC}&=4\underset{\sim}{a}-2\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{AC}&=2(2\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b})\end{aligned}$$

Therefore $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is parallel to $2\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$ because it is a scalar multiple.

children.prompt:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PR}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}-\overrightarrow{RQ}\\\overrightarrow{PR}&=(6\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})-(2\underset{\sim}{a}+5\underset{\sim}{b})\\\overrightarrow{PR}&=4\underset{\sim}{a}-4\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{PR}&=-4(\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a})\end{aligned}$$

Therefore $\overrightarrow{PR}$ is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}$ because it is a scalar multiple, with opposite direction.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{PR}=\frac53\overrightarrow{PQ}$. The vectors are parallel and share point $P$, so $P,Q,R$ are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PQ}&=3\underset{\sim}{p}+9\underset{\sim}{q}\\&=3(\underset{\sim}{p}+3\underset{\sim}{q})\\\overrightarrow{PR}&=5\underset{\sim}{p}+15\underset{\sim}{q}\\&=5(\underset{\sim}{p}+3\underset{\sim}{q})\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt:
The diagram shows congruent parallelograms.

Let $\overrightarrow{BE}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=\underset{\sim}{b}$.

Prove that $A,E,I$ lie on a straight line.

spec.description: Four congruent parallelograms in an oblique two-by-two grid. The A–E–I diagonal is not drawn. Vector arrows B to E and B to C carry under-tilde labels a and b.
spec.mathematics: Rows A,D,G; B,E,H; C,F,I are parallel and equally divided. Columns A,B,C; D,E,F; G,H,I are parallel and equally divided.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AE}=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}=\overrightarrow{EI}$. These vectors are parallel and share $E$, so $A,E,I$ lie on a straight line.
answer.worked:
Corresponding sides of the congruent parallelograms give $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{EF}=\underset{\sim}{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{FI}=\overrightarrow{BE}=\underset{\sim}{a}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AE}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BE}\\&=\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a}\\\overrightarrow{EI}&=\overrightarrow{EF}+\overrightarrow{FI}\\&=\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a}\end{aligned}$$
Thus $\overrightarrow{AE}=\overrightarrow{EI}$. They are parallel and share the common point $E$, so $A,E,I$ are collinear.

content.prompt: The triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(2\sqrt3,3)$, $B(3\sqrt3,4)$ and $C(2\sqrt3,5)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OA}&=\begin{pmatrix}2\sqrt3\\3\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{OB}&=\begin{pmatrix}3\sqrt3\\4\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{OC}&=\begin{pmatrix}2\sqrt3\\5\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}3\sqrt3-2\sqrt3\\4-3\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt3\\1\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{CB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OC}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}3\sqrt3-2\sqrt3\\4-5\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt3\\-1\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{AB}|&=\sqrt{(\sqrt3)^2+1^2}\\&=2\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{CB}|&=\sqrt{(\sqrt3)^2+(-1)^2}\\&=2\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{AC}|&=\sqrt{0^2+2^2}\\&=2\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}\\\overrightarrow{AP}&=\overrightarrow{OP}-\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{a}\end{align*}$$
Given $\overrightarrow{AP}=k\overrightarrow{AB}$,
$$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{a}&=k(\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a})\\\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{a}&=k\underset{\sim}{b}-k\underset{\sim}{a}\\\underset{\sim}{p}&=\underset{\sim}{a}-k\underset{\sim}{a}+k\underset{\sim}{b}\\\underset{\sim}{p}&=(1-k)\underset{\sim}{a}+k\underset{\sim}{b}\end{align*}$$

Let $\underset{\sim}{u}=\overrightarrow{AM}$, $\underset{\sim}{v}=\overrightarrow{PN}$, $\underset{\sim}{a}=\overrightarrow{AP}$, $\underset{\sim}{b}=\overrightarrow{BQ}$ and $\underset{\sim}{p}=\overrightarrow{MN}$.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral ABQP with midpoint segment MN; all six labels and no arrows or ticks.
spec.mathematics: M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of PQ. AP, MN and BQ are horizontal in the source illustration; no additional parallelism is asserted.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AM}$ and $\overrightarrow{MB}$ have the same length and direction. Similarly, $\overrightarrow{PN}$ and $\overrightarrow{NQ}$ have the same length and direction.
answer.worked: Since $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $\overrightarrow{AM}$ and $\overrightarrow{MB}$ have the same length and direction, so $\overrightarrow{MB}=\underset{\sim}{u}$. Similarly, since $N$ is the midpoint of $PQ$, $\overrightarrow{PN}$ and $\overrightarrow{NQ}$ have the same length and direction, so $\overrightarrow{NQ}=\underset{\sim}{v}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$ in terms of $\underset{\sim}{p}$, $\underset{\sim}{u}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AN}&=\overrightarrow{AP}+\overrightarrow{PN}\\\overrightarrow{AN}&=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{v}\\\overrightarrow{AN}&=\overrightarrow{AM}+\overrightarrow{MN}\\\overrightarrow{AN}&=\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{p}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{v}&=\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{p}\\\underset{\sim}{a}&=\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{u}-\underset{\sim}{v}.\end{aligned}$$
Similarly,
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MQ}&=\overrightarrow{MB}+\overrightarrow{BQ}\\\overrightarrow{MQ}&=\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{MQ}&=\overrightarrow{MN}+\overrightarrow{NQ}\\\overrightarrow{MQ}&=\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{v}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{b}&=\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{v}\\\underset{\sim}{b}&=\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{v}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}&=\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{u}-\underset{\sim}{v}+(\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{v})\\\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}&=2\underset{\sim}{p}.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{BC}&=\overrightarrow{AC}-\overrightarrow{AB}\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=2\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=\overrightarrow{MB}+\overrightarrow{BN}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}+\tfrac34(2\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a})\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=-\tfrac14\underset{\sim}{a}+\tfrac32\underset{\sim}{b}\end{aligned}$$

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{MD}=2\overrightarrow{MN}$. These vectors are parallel and share M, so M, N and D are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MN}&=-\tfrac14\underset{\sim}{a}+\tfrac32\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=-\tfrac14(\underset{\sim}{a}-6\underset{\sim}{b})\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=\overrightarrow{MA}+\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CD}\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=-\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}+2\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=-\tfrac12(\underset{\sim}{a}-6\underset{\sim}{b})\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=2\overrightarrow{MN}\end{aligned}$$
The vectors $\overrightarrow{MN}$ and $\overrightarrow{MD}$ are parallel and share the common point M. Therefore M, N and D are collinear.

content.prompt:
The triangle $PQR$ is shown. $M$ is the midpoint of $QR$.

$\overrightarrow{PR}=\underset{\sim}{x},\quad \overrightarrow{PQ}=\underset{\sim}{y}$.

$\overrightarrow{PO}:\overrightarrow{OM}=3:2$.

$\overrightarrow{PN}$ can be written in the form $k\underset{\sim}{x}$.

Work out the value of $k$.

spec.description: Outline triangle PQR with horizontal PR, Q above, midpoint M on QR, N on PR, and segments PM and QN intersecting at O. All six labels are retained. No arrowheads, midpoint ticks or numerical dimensions.
spec.mathematics: M=(Q+R)/2; O=P+(3/5)(M-P); N is the intersection of QO with PR. Coordinates implement these relationships without printing additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry is supplied in the question; no solution annotations or scalar value are shown.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PR}&=\underset{\sim}{x},\quad \overrightarrow{PQ}=\underset{\sim}{y}\\\overrightarrow{QR}&=\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y}\\\overrightarrow{QM}&=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PM}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QM}\\\overrightarrow{PM}&=\underset{\sim}{y}+\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\\\overrightarrow{PM}&=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})\end{aligned}$

Since $PO:OM=3:2$,

$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PO}&=\frac35\left[\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})\right]\\\overrightarrow{PO}&=\frac3{10}(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})\end{aligned}$

Since $Q,O,N$ are collinear, write $\overrightarrow{QO}=m\overrightarrow{QN}$.

$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PO}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QO}\\\overrightarrow{PO}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+m\overrightarrow{QN}\\\frac3{10}(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})&=\underset{\sim}{y}+m(k\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\\\frac3{10}\underset{\sim}{x}+\frac3{10}\underset{\sim}{y}&=mk\underset{\sim}{x}+(1-m)\underset{\sim}{y}\end{aligned}$

Comparing coefficients:

$\begin{aligned}mk&=\frac3{10}\\1-m&=\frac3{10}\\m&=\frac7{10}\\k&=\frac37\end{aligned}$

The answer is (C).

content.prompt: Find the exact magnitude and direction (to the nearest degree) of vector $\vec{AB}$ where $\vec{OA}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\ 1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{OB}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\ -1\end{pmatrix}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\vec{AB} &= \vec{OB} - \vec{OA} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix}3\\ -1\end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix}2\\ 1\end{pmatrix} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix}1\\ -2\end{pmatrix}
\end{align*}$$
$$|\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{1^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{5}$$
The vector points into the fourth quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}
A &= \tan^{-1}(2)\approx 63.43^\circ \\
\theta &= 360^\circ - 63.43^\circ\approx 297^\circ
\end{align*}$$
The magnitude is $\sqrt{5}$ and the direction is $297^\circ$.

content.prompt:
Kylie drives her car from the origin all along the vector $\vec{OA}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\5\end{pmatrix}$.
Then from $A$ she drives all along the vector $\vec{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and after that, from $B$ she drove to $C$ along the vector $\vec{BC}=\begin{pmatrix}p\\p+2\end{pmatrix}$, where $p$ is a positive constant.
Given that the vector position $\vec{OC}$ from her starting to her final position has a magnitude of $13$, what is the value of $p$?
(A) $5$
(B) $2$
(C) $3$
(D) $1$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\vec{OC} &= \vec{OA}+\vec{AB}+\vec{BC} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix}6\\5\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}-3\\3\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}p\\p+2\end{pmatrix} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix}p+3\\p+10\end{pmatrix}
\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}
(p+3)^2+(p+10)^2 &= 13^2 \\
2p^2+26p-60 &= 0 \\
p^2+13p-30 &= 0 \\
(p+15)(p-2) &= 0
\end{align*}$$
Since $p$ is positive, $p=2$.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows a Cartesian plane where the points $A$ and $B$ have the position vectors $\vec{OA}=-2\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$ and $\vec{OB}=6\mathbf{i}-7\mathbf{j}$, respectively, and $O$ is the origin.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\\&=(6\mathbf{i}-7\mathbf{j})-(-2\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})\\&=8\mathbf{i}-12\mathbf{j}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt:
The point $P$ lies on the interval $AB$ with $AP:PB=3:1$.
Use vector methods to find the coordinates of $P$.

answer.worked:
Since $AP:PB=3:1$, point $P$ is $\frac{3}{4}$ of the way from $A$ to $B$.
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{OP}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\frac{3}{4}\overrightarrow{AB}\\&=-2\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}+\frac{3}{4}(8\mathbf{i}-12\mathbf{j})\\&=-2\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}+6\mathbf{i}-9\mathbf{j}\\&=4\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}\end{align*}$$
The coordinates of $P$ are $(4,-4)$.

content.prompt:
In the following diagram, $M$ is the midpoint of line segment $AB$, and $\vec{ON}=\frac{4}{5}\vec{OM}$.
It is given that $\vec{OA}=\mathbf{a}$ and $\vec{OB}=\mathbf{b}$.
Which of the following expressions correctly relates $\vec{NM}$ with $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$?
(A) $\vec{NM}=\frac{4}{5}(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b})$
(B) $\vec{NM}=\frac{2}{5}(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})$
(C) $\vec{NM}=\frac{1}{10}(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})$
(D) $\vec{NM}=\frac{1}{10}(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b})$

answer.worked:
Since $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$:
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{OM}&=\frac{1}{2}(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})\end{align*}$$
Also $\overrightarrow{ON}=\frac{4}{5}\overrightarrow{OM}$, so
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{NM}&=\overrightarrow{OM}-\overrightarrow{ON}\\&=\frac{1}{5}\overrightarrow{OM}\\&=\frac{1}{10}(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})\end{align*}$$
The answer is C.

content.prompt:
In the diagram below, $OABC$ is a parallelogram.
$\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\underset{\sim}{c}$.
$P$ is the point on $AB$ such that $AP=\frac{1}{4}AB$.
$Q$ is the point on $OC$ such that $OQ=\frac{2}{3}OC$.
Find $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ in terms of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{c}$, giving your answer in simplest form.

answer.worked:
Since $OABC$ is a parallelogram, $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OC}=\underset{\sim}{c}$.
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{AP}&=\frac{1}{4}\underset{\sim}{c}\\\overrightarrow{OQ}&=\frac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{c}\\\overrightarrow{OP}&=\underset{\sim}{a}+\frac{1}{4}\underset{\sim}{c}\end{align*}$$
Therefore
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{PQ}&=\overrightarrow{OQ}-\overrightarrow{OP}\\&=\frac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{c}-\left(\underset{\sim}{a}+\frac{1}{4}\underset{\sim}{c}\right)\\&=-\underset{\sim}{a}+\left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{4}\right)\underset{\sim}{c}\\&=-\underset{\sim}{a}+\frac{5}{12}\underset{\sim}{c}\end{align*}$$

A scalar quantity has only size, or magnitude.
E.g. Distance of school from home is 3 km.
Speed of a plane is 800 km/h.
Temperature, length, area, …

A vector quantity has magnitude and direction.
E.g. Displacement of school from home is 3 km at a bearing of 120°.
Velocity of a plane is 800 km/h at a bearing of 225°.
Acceleration, force, weight, …

A vector quantity is often used to represent movement or change.

entries.description: Given that \(\underset{\sim}{a}=\binom{2}{-2}\), \(\underset{\sim}{b}=\binom{-3}{-5}\) and \(\underset{\sim}{c}=\binom{24}{8}\), find the values of \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) such that \(\underset{\sim}{c}=\lambda_1\underset{\sim}{a}+\lambda_2\underset{\sim}{b}\).
entries.presentation: Prompt spans two lines. Preserve vector undertildes and space for simultaneous-equation working.

entries.description:
Supplied working, in order:
\(\underset{\sim}{c}=\lambda_1\underset{\sim}{a}+\lambda_2\underset{\sim}{b}\)
\(\binom{24}{8}=\lambda_1\binom{2}{-2}+\lambda_2\binom{-3}{-5}\)
\(\binom{24}{8}=\binom{2\lambda_1-3\lambda_2}{-2\lambda_1-5\lambda_2}\)
\(2\lambda_1-3\lambda_2=24\quad(1)\)
\(-2\lambda_1-5\lambda_2=8\quad(2)\)
Adding (1) and (2):
\(-8\lambda_2=32\)
\(\lambda_2=-4\)
Substitute \(\lambda_2=-4\) into (1):
\(2\lambda_1-3(-4)=24\)
\(2\lambda_1+12=24\)
\(\lambda_1=6\)

entries.description:
pa+b = \begin{pmatrix}3p+1\\-2p+4\end{pmatrix} = k\begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix}
3p+1 = 7k (1)
-2p+4 = 2k (2)
rearranging (2): k = (-2p+4)/2
sub k into (1): 3p+1 = 7(-2p+4)/2
2(3p+1) = 7(-2p+4)
6p+2 = -14p+28
20p = 26
p = 13/10

entries.description: Find the value of q such that a + qb is perpendicular to \begin{pmatrix}5\\1\end{pmatrix}.

Perpendicular if \begin{pmatrix}1\\-5\end{pmatrix} or \begin{pmatrix}-1\\5\end{pmatrix}
Using \begin{pmatrix}1\\-5\end{pmatrix}: 3+q = k
-2+4q = -5k
Substitute k = 3+q:

-2+4q = -15-5q
9q = -13
q = -13/9

entries.description:
Just like column vector notation, to add or subtract vectors, add or subtract each component.
\mathbf a=x_1\mathbf i+y_1\mathbf j
\mathbf b=x_2\mathbf i+y_2\mathbf j
\mathbf a+\mathbf b=(x_1+x_2)\mathbf i+(y_1+y_2)\mathbf j
To multiply a vector by a scalar, multiply each component separately.
\mathbf a=x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j
\lambda\mathbf a=\lambda(x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j)
\phantom{\lambda\mathbf a}=\lambda x\mathbf i+\lambda y\mathbf j

entries.description:
Triangle Law of Addition
\(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}\)
When two vectors are placed head-to-tail, the resultant vector connects the tail of the first vector to the head of the second vector.

entries.description:
Parallelogram Law of Subtraction
\(\overrightarrow{AB}-\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{DB}\)
The difference between two vectors equals the vector from the head of the second vector to the head of the first vector.

\(\overrightarrow{BC}=\begin{pmatrix}8\\k\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}5\\7\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\k-7\end{pmatrix}\)

The parallelogram WXYZ has vertices W(−6, 4), X(6, 2), Y(4, 9) and Z(a, b).

\(\overrightarrow{WZ}=\overrightarrow{XY}\)
\(\begin{pmatrix}a+6\\b-4\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\7\end{pmatrix}\)
\(a+6=-2\)
\(a=-8\)
\(b-4=7\)
\(b=11\).

entries.description:
Supplied blue worked solution, in source order:
\(\overrightarrow{PR}=x,\ \overrightarrow{PQ}=y\)
\(\overrightarrow{QR}=x-y\)
\(\overrightarrow{QM}=\frac12(x-y)\)

\(\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QM}=\overrightarrow{PM}\)
\(y+\frac12(x-y)=\overrightarrow{PM}\)
\(\therefore\ \overrightarrow{PM}=\frac12(x+y)\)

\(\overrightarrow{PO}=\frac35(\frac12x+y)=\frac3{10}(x+y)\)
\(\overrightarrow{PO}=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QO}\)
\(\overrightarrow{PO}=\overrightarrow{PQ}+m\times\overrightarrow{QN}\)
\(\frac3{10}(x+y)=y+m(kx-y)\)
\(\therefore\ \frac3{10}x+\frac3{10}y=mkx+(1-m)y\)
Comparing coefficients:
\(mk=\frac3{10}\)
\(1-m=\frac3{10}\)
\(m=\frac7{10}\)
\(\therefore\ k=\frac37\)
